questions.question: Which of the below is a best-practice when designing solutions on AWS?

options.text: Invest heavily in architecting your environment, as it is not easy to change your design later.

explanation.summary: AWS architectures are designed to be flexible and change-friendly, so heavy upfront design is not a best practice.
explanation.why: AWS encourages iterative design and continuous improvement. Cloud resources are elastic and programmable, allowing architectures to evolve easily over time. Over-investing in upfront design reduces agility and conflicts with cloud-native principles such as experimentation and rapid iteration.

options.text: Use AWS reservations to reduce costs when testing your production environment.

explanation.summary: Reservations are intended for steady-state production workloads, not short-lived testing environments.
explanation.why: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans require long-term commitments. Test environments are typically variable and short-term, making On-Demand pricing more appropriate. Using reservations for testing can lead to unnecessary costs and unused capacity.

options.text: Automate wherever possible to make architectural (© ) experimentation easier.

explanation.summary: Automation enables fast, repeatable, and low-risk experimentation when designing AWS architectures.
keyPoints: Automation reduces human error and manual effort
Infrastructure can be provisioned and modified consistently
Enables rollback and recovery through versioned templates
Aligns with Infrastructure as Code best practices
examples: Using AWS CloudFormation to deploy and tear down environments
Automating scaling rules with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
Using CI/CD pipelines to test architectural changes
explanation.additionalInfo: Automation is a core design principle of the AWS Well-Architected Framework. By treating infrastructure as code, teams can safely test architectural changes, reduce deployment risk, and improve operational efficiency. Automated environments are easier to audit, reproduce, and scale, making them ideal for both experimentation and production workloads.

options.text: Provision a large compute capacity to handle any spikes in load

explanation.summary: Overprovisioning compute capacity contradicts AWS elasticity and cost-optimization principles.
explanation.why: AWS provides Auto Scaling to dynamically adjust capacity based on demand. Pre-provisioning large amounts of compute leads to wasted resources and higher costs. Designing for elasticity is preferred over static overprovisioning.

questions.question: According to the AWS Acceptable Use Policy, which of the following statements is true regarding penetration testing of EC2 instances?

options.text: Penetration testing is not allowed in AWS.

explanation.summary: AWS allows penetration testing under defined conditions.
explanation.why: AWS explicitly permits customers to perform penetration testing on certain services. Saying it is not allowed contradicts AWS policy and is a common exam trap.

options.text: Penetration testing is performed automatically by AWS to determine vulnerabilities in your AWS infrastructure.

explanation.summary: AWS does not automatically perform penetration testing on customer resources.
explanation.why: While AWS secures the underlying infrastructure, customers are responsible for testing the security of their own workloads. AWS does not conduct penetration testing on behalf of customers.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Security Best Practices Shared

options.text: Penetration testing can be performed by the customer on their own instances without prior authorization from AWS.

explanation.summary: AWS allows customers to perform penetration testing on their own EC2 instances without prior approval.
keyPoints: No prior approval required for approved services
Testing must follow AWS Acceptable Use Policy
Only customer-owned resources may be tested
Applies to EC2 and other supported services
examples: Running vulnerability scans against your EC2 instances
Testing application security controls hosted on EC2
Performing network penetration tests within your VPC
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS supports responsible security testing to help customers validate the security of their workloads. Customers must ensure tests do not impact other tenants or AWS infrastructure. Some attack simulations, such as DDoS testing, require explicit approval. Understanding these boundaries is critical for both security operations and AWS certification exams.

options.text: The AWS customers are only allowed to perform penetration testing on services managed by AWS.

explanation.summary: Customers are allowed to test their own workloads, not AWS-managed infrastructure.
explanation.why: AWS-managed services are covered by AWS security controls. Customers are responsible for testing their own instances and applications, not AWS-owned infrastructure.

questions.question: Which service is used to ensure that messages between software components are not lost if one or more components fail?

explanation.summary: Amazon SQS provides durable message queuing that decouples components and prevents message loss.
keyPoints: Stores messages redundantly across multiple Availability Zones
examples: Queueing orders between a web tier and processing workers
Buffering traffic spikes for backend services
Ensuring messages persist during consumer failures
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon SQS is designed for reliability and scalability in distributed systems. Messages are retained until processed and deleted, allowing downstream components to recover without data loss. This makes SQS a foundational service for decoupled, fault-tolerant AWS architectures and a frequent topic in certification exams.

explanation.summary: Amazon SES is an email sending service, not a message queue.
explanation.why: SES is designed for sending transactional and marketing emails. It does not provide message persistence or decoupling between application components.

explanation.summary: AWS Direct Connect provides private network connectivity, not message durability.
explanation.why: Direct Connect improves network performance and reliability between on-premises environments and AWS, but it does not store or manage application messages.

explanation.summary: Amazon Connect is a cloud-based contact center service.
explanation.why: Amazon Connect is used for customer support workflows and call handling. It does not function as a general-purpose message queue for application components.

questions.question: The principle 'design for failure and nothing will fail' is very important when designing your AWS Cloud architecture. Which of the following would help adhere to this principle? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Multi-factor authentication strengthens security but does not directly support fault tolerance or failure resilience.
explanation.why: MFA protects identities by requiring additional authentication factors. It does not address system availability, redundancy, or failure handling, which are core to designing for failure.

explanation.summary: Availability Zones enable workloads to continue operating even if one data center fails.
keyPoints: Physically separate data centers within a Region
Designed for isolation and fault containment
Reduce blast radius of infrastructure failures
examples: Running EC2 instances across multiple AZs
explanation.additionalInfo: Designing across multiple Availability Zones is a foundational AWS best practice. AZ-level isolation ensures that power, cooling, and networking failures in one data center do not impact workloads in others, allowing applications to remain available during failures.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancing automatically routes traffic away from failed resources.
keyPoints: Automatically stops sending traffic to failed instances
examples: Routing traffic only to healthy EC2 instances
Handling instance failures without user impact
explanation.additionalInfo: Elastic Load Balancing is a critical component of fault-tolerant architectures. By combining ELB with Auto Scaling and multi-AZ deployments, applications can withstand instance and AZ failures without service disruption.

explanation.summary: Penetration testing focuses on security posture, not system failure handling.
explanation.why: Penetration testing identifies vulnerabilities but does not contribute to availability, redundancy, or resilience against infrastructure failures.

explanation.summary: Vertical scaling increases instance size but introduces single points of failure.
explanation.why: Scaling up a single resource improves capacity but does not protect against failures. Fault-tolerant designs favor horizontal scaling across multiple resources.

questions.question: What is the AWS service that provides a virtual network dedicated to your AWS account?

explanation.summary: AWS VPN provides secure connectivity, not a dedicated virtual network.
explanation.why: AWS VPN connects on-premises networks to AWS but does not create the virtual network itself.

explanation.summary: Subnets are components within a virtual network, not the network itself.
explanation.why: Subnets divide a VPC into smaller address ranges. They cannot exist independently without a VPC.

explanation.summary: Dedicated Hosts provide physical server isolation, not network isolation.
explanation.why: Dedicated Hosts control how instances are placed on physical servers. They do not define networking boundaries.

explanation.summary: Amazon VPC provides a logically isolated virtual network dedicated to your AWS account.
keyPoints: Logically isolated from other AWS customers
Allows control over subnets and routing
Enables network security with security groups and NACLs
examples: Launching EC2 instances in isolated networks
Connecting to on-premises networks using VPN or Direct Connect
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon VPC is the core networking service in AWS. It gives customers full control over their virtual networking environment, including IP addressing, routing, gateways, and security controls, making it essential for secure and scalable cloud architectures.

questions.question: According to the AWS Shared responsibility model, which of the following are the responsibility of the customer? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Managing environmental events of AWS data centers.

explanation.summary: AWS manages physical data center operations and environmental controls.
explanation.why: Environmental controls such as power, cooling, and physical facility protection are part of AWS’s responsibility under the shared responsibility model.

options.text: Protecting the confidentiality of data in transit in Amazon S3.

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for protecting their data through encryption and secure access.
keyPoints: Applies to all stored and transmitted data
examples: Enabling bucket policies to restrict access
Using AWS KMS for encryption keys
explanation.additionalInfo: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS secures the infrastructure, while customers are responsible for securing their data. This includes encrypting data in transit and ensuring secure access to Amazon S3 resources.

options.text: Controlling physical access to AWS Regions.

explanation.summary: AWS is responsible for physical security of its facilities.
explanation.why: Customers do not manage physical access to AWS Regions or data centers. This is fully handled by AWS.

options.text: Ensuring that the underlying EC2 host is configured properly.

explanation.summary: AWS manages the underlying infrastructure and host configuration.
explanation.why: The hypervisor and physical host configuration are AWS responsibilities. Customers manage the guest operating system and applications only.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Security Best Practices Shared

options.text: Patching applications installed on Amazon EC2.

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for maintaining and patching their applications.
keyPoints: Applies to software installed on EC2
Part of security in the cloud
examples: Applying security patches to web servers
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS provides the infrastructure, but customers retain full responsibility for securing and maintaining the software they install. Failure to patch applications is a common cause of security incidents.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services can be used as a compute resource? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Amazon VPC is a networking service, not a compute resource.
explanation.why: VPC provides network isolation, routing, and security boundaries. It does not execute code or provide processing power.

explanation.summary: Amazon CloudWatch is a monitoring and observability service.
explanation.why: CloudWatch collects metrics, logs, and events. It does not run applications or provide compute capacity.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is an object storage service, not a compute service.
explanation.why: S3 stores data and does not execute code or process workloads.

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 provides resizable virtual servers for running applications.
keyPoints: Provides virtual machines in the cloud
Supports full control of operating system
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon EC2 is a core AWS compute service that offers flexibility, scalability, and control. Customers manage the OS and applications while AWS manages the underlying infrastructure.

explanation.summary: AWS Lambda provides serverless compute for running code without managing servers.
keyPoints: Runs code in response to events
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Lambda abstracts infrastructure management, allowing developers to focus solely on code. It is a fundamental serverless compute service in AWS.

questions.question: Your company is designing a new application that will store and retrieve photos and videos. Which of the following services should you recommend as the underlying storage mechanism?

explanation.summary: Amazon EBS provides block storage for EC2, not scalable object storage.
explanation.why: EBS volumes are attached to individual EC2 instances and are not optimized for large-scale object storage or global access patterns.

explanation.summary: Amazon SQS is a messaging service, not a storage solution for media files.
explanation.why: SQS stores messages temporarily and is not designed for storing large binary objects like photos or videos.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is designed for durable, scalable object storage.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon S3 is the preferred storage service for unstructured data such as photos and videos. It offers virtually unlimited scalability and eleven nines of durability.

explanation.summary: Instance store provides temporary storage tied to an EC2 instance lifecycle.
explanation.why: Data in instance store is lost when the instance stops or terminates, making it unsuitable for durable media storage.

questions.question: Which of the following is equivalent to a user name and password and is used to authenticate your programmatic access to AWS services and APIs?

explanation.summary: EC2 instance passwords are not used for AWS API authentication.
explanation.why: Instance passwords are related to operating system access, not AWS service authentication.

explanation.summary: Key pairs are used for SSH access to EC2 instances.
explanation.why: Key pairs authenticate to instances, not AWS APIs.

explanation.summary: Access keys authenticate programmatic access to AWS services.
keyPoints: Consist of access key ID and secret access key
Used with AWS CLI, SDKs, and APIs
Associated with IAM users or roles
explanation.additionalInfo: Access keys provide programmatic access to AWS. Best practices recommend using IAM roles instead of long-term access keys whenever possible.

explanation.summary: MFA adds an extra layer of security but does not replace access keys.
explanation.why: MFA enhances authentication but is not used alone for programmatic API access.

questions.question: What does Amazon ElastiCache provide?

explanation.summary: Amazon ElastiCache provides fully managed in-memory caching to improve application performance.
examples: Storing session data for web applications
Improving read performance for frequently accessed data
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon ElastiCache is commonly used to offload read traffic from databases such as Amazon RDS and DynamoDB. By keeping frequently accessed data in memory, it significantly reduces latency and improves throughput for read-heavy workloads.

options.text: An Ehcache compatible in-memory data store.

explanation.summary: Amazon ElastiCache does not provide Ehcache compatibility.
explanation.why: ElastiCache supports Redis and Memcached engines only. Ehcache is a separate caching technology not natively supported by ElastiCache.

options.text: An online software store that allows Customers to launch pre-configured software with just few clicks.

explanation.summary: This describes AWS Marketplace, not Amazon ElastiCache.
explanation.why: AWS Marketplace is used to deploy pre-configured software solutions, while ElastiCache is an in-memory caching service.

options.text: A domain name system in the cloud.

explanation.summary: Cloud DNS services are provided by Amazon Route 53, not ElastiCache.
explanation.why: Amazon Route 53 is AWS’s DNS service. ElastiCache is focused solely on in-memory caching.

questions.question: What is the AWS service that enables you to manage all of your AWS accounts from a single master account?

explanation.summary: AWS WAF protects web applications but does not manage AWS accounts.
explanation.why: AWS WAF is a security service used to filter web traffic. It does not provide multi-account management.

explanation.summary: AWS Trusted Advisor provides recommendations, not account management.
explanation.why: Trusted Advisor analyzes AWS environments and provides best practice checks but does not control or manage accounts.

explanation.summary: AWS Organizations enables centralized management of multiple AWS accounts.
examples: Managing separate dev, test, and prod accounts
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Organizations is essential for enterprises using multiple AWS accounts. It enables governance, security controls, and cost management at scale through centralized policies and consolidated billing.

explanation.summary: Amazon Config tracks configuration changes but does not manage accounts.
explanation.why: Config records resource configuration history and compliance status but does not provide centralized account control.

questions.question: Which of the following EC2 instance purchasing options supports the Bring Your Own License (BYOL) model for almost every BYOL scenario?

explanation.summary: Dedicated Instances provide hardware isolation but limited visibility for licensing requirements.
explanation.why: Dedicated Instances do not provide full control over physical cores and sockets, which is often required for BYOL compliance.

explanation.summary: Dedicated Hosts provide full visibility and control required for BYOL licensing.
keyPoints: Physical server dedicated to one customer
examples: Deploying Windows Server with custom licenses
explanation.additionalInfo: Dedicated Hosts are designed for scenarios where software licensing is tied to physical hardware attributes. They allow customers to reuse existing licenses while meeting vendor compliance requirements.

explanation.summary: On-Demand Instances do not meet most BYOL licensing requirements.
explanation.why: On-Demand Instances abstract underlying hardware, which limits license portability for many enterprise software vendors.

explanation.summary: Reserved Instances are a billing discount model, not a licensing model.
explanation.why: Reserved Instances reduce cost but do not provide physical host control required for BYOL compliance.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the benefits of moving infrastructure from an on-premises data center to AWS?

options.text: Free support for all enterprise customers.

explanation.summary: AWS support plans are paid services and not automatically free for enterprise customers.
explanation.why: Enterprise Support requires a paid subscription. AWS does not provide free enterprise-level support by default.

explanation.summary: Data protection in AWS requires customer configuration and responsibility.
explanation.why: AWS provides tools for data protection, but customers must configure encryption, backups, and access controls themselves.

explanation.summary: AWS eliminates the need for upfront hardware investments, reducing CapEx.
keyPoints: No need to purchase physical servers
Shift from CapEx to OpEx model
Pay only for what you use
examples: Launching new workloads without buying hardware
Scaling environments without data center expansion
explanation.additionalInfo: By moving to AWS, organizations avoid large upfront capital investments in hardware and facilities. Instead, they adopt an operational expense model that aligns costs directly with usage and business demand.

options.text: AWS holds responsibility for managing customer applications.

explanation.summary: Customers remain responsible for their applications under the shared responsibility model.
explanation.why: AWS manages the infrastructure, but customers are responsible for application code, configuration, and security.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Security Best Practices Shared

questions.question: Which of the following are important design principles you should adopt when designing systems on AWS? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Always use Global Services in your architecture rather than Regional Services.

explanation.summary: AWS architectures commonly rely on Regional services for resiliency and compliance.
explanation.why: Not all services are global, and Regional services provide better control over availability, latency, and compliance requirements.

options.text: Always choose to pay as you go.

explanation.summary: Pay-as-you-go is an AWS pricing model, not a design principle.
explanation.why: Design principles focus on architecture and reliability rather than billing strategies.

explanation.summary: AWS encourages treating servers as disposable resources.
explanation.why: Cloud-native design favors immutable infrastructure and automated replacement rather than fixed servers.

explanation.summary: Automation improves consistency, scalability, and operational efficiency.
explanation.additionalInfo: Automation is central to cloud-native design. It enables repeatable processes, reduces human error, and allows systems to respond dynamically to change.

explanation.summary: Eliminating single points of failure improves system availability and resilience.
explanation.additionalInfo: Removing single points of failure ensures that no single component outage can bring down an entire system, which is a core AWS architectural best practice.

questions.question: Which AWS Service can be used to establish a dedicated, private network connection between AWS and your datacenter?

explanation.summary: AWS Direct Connect provides a private, dedicated network connection to AWS.
examples: Connecting on-premises data centers to AWS
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Direct Connect is commonly used for hybrid cloud environments where predictable performance and private connectivity are required.

explanation.summary: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network, not a private network connection.
explanation.why: CloudFront improves content delivery to end users but does not establish private connectivity between networks.

explanation.summary: AWS Snowball is used for offline data transfer, not network connectivity.
explanation.why: Snowball devices move data physically and do not provide continuous network connections.

explanation.summary: Amazon Route 53 is a DNS service.
explanation.why: Route 53 manages domain names and routing, not private network connections.

questions.question: You are working on two projects that require completely different network configurations. Which AWS service or feature will allow you to isolate resources and network configurations?

explanation.summary: Internet gateways provide internet access, not resource isolation.
explanation.why: An internet gateway enables communication between a VPC and the internet. It does not isolate environments or define separate network boundaries.

explanation.summary: Amazon VPC allows complete isolation of network environments.
keyPoints: Logical isolation at the network level
examples: Using separate VPCs for different projects
Applying distinct security policies per project
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon VPC is the primary AWS service for isolating network configurations. Separate VPCs ensure that routing tables, subnets, gateways, and security rules do not overlap unless explicitly connected.

explanation.summary: Security groups control traffic, not full network isolation.
explanation.why: Security groups act as virtual firewalls within a VPC. They cannot isolate entire network environments.

explanation.summary: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network service.
explanation.why: CloudFront improves content delivery performance and does not provide network isolation.

questions.question: Which of the following services can help protect your web applications from SQL injection and other vulnerabilities in your application code?

explanation.summary: Amazon Cognito provides authentication and identity management.
explanation.why: Cognito manages user sign-up and authentication but does not inspect or filter web traffic for application-layer attacks.

explanation.summary: AWS IAM controls access to AWS resources, not application traffic.
explanation.why: IAM governs permissions for users and services. It does not protect against SQL injection or application-layer exploits.

explanation.summary: Amazon Aurora is a relational database service.
explanation.why: Aurora stores data but does not provide web application firewall capabilities.

explanation.summary: AWS WAF protects web applications from common web exploits.
keyPoints: Filters malicious HTTP and HTTPS requests
Protects against SQL injection and XSS
Integrates with CloudFront, ALB, and API Gateway
Supports custom and managed rule sets
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS WAF is a core security service for application-layer protection. It allows fine-grained control over incoming traffic and is commonly used to secure public-facing web applications.

questions.question: An organization needs to analyze and process a large number of data sets. Which AWS service should they use?

explanation.summary: Amazon EMR is designed for large-scale data processing.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon EMR simplifies running big data frameworks on AWS. It is optimized for processing large datasets efficiently and is commonly used for analytics and machine learning workloads.

explanation.summary: Amazon MQ is a managed message broker service.
explanation.why: Amazon MQ supports message-oriented middleware and is not designed for large-scale data analytics.

explanation.summary: Amazon SNS is a messaging and notification service.
explanation.why: SNS distributes messages to subscribers but does not process or analyze large datasets.

explanation.summary: Amazon SQS is a message queue service.
explanation.why: SQS decouples system components but does not provide data analytics capabilities.

questions.question: Based on the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following are the sole responsibility of AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Monitoring application and network performance is a shared or customer responsibility depending on the layer.
explanation.why: Customers are responsible for monitoring the performance of their workloads and applications. AWS provides tools, but usage and configuration are customer-managed.

explanation.summary: Installing and managing software on EC2 is the customer’s responsibility.
explanation.why: Under IaaS, customers manage the guest operating system and installed software.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Security Best Practices Shared

explanation.summary: AWS is fully responsible for the hypervisor layer.
keyPoints: Part of security of the cloud
explanation.additionalInfo: The hypervisor is a foundational component of AWS infrastructure. Customers never access or manage it, making it a sole AWS responsibility.

explanation.summary: Network ACL configuration is managed by the customer.
explanation.why: Customers define NACL rules within their VPC to control traffic flow.

explanation.summary: AWS manages and maintains all physical hardware.
explanation.additionalInfo: Physical infrastructure management is entirely handled by AWS, allowing customers to focus on workloads rather than data center operations.

questions.question: What is the AWS service that provides you the highest level of control over the underlying virtual infrastructure?

explanation.summary: Amazon Redshift is a managed data warehouse service.
explanation.why: Redshift abstracts infrastructure management and does not offer low-level control over virtual machines.

explanation.summary: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database.
explanation.why: DynamoDB hides infrastructure details and does not provide OS or instance-level control.

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 gives customers maximum control over virtual machines.
explanation.additionalInfo: Among AWS services, EC2 offers the highest degree of control short of managing physical hardware. This makes it suitable for custom or legacy workloads.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS is a managed database service.
explanation.why: RDS abstracts OS and database engine management, reducing customer control.

questions.question: What are the default security credentials that are required to access the AWS management console for an IAM user account?

explanation.summary: MFA is optional and enhances security but is not required by default.
explanation.why: IAM users can sign in without MFA unless explicitly enforced.

explanation.summary: Security tokens are temporary credentials, not default console login requirements.
explanation.why: They are typically used with assumed roles or federation.

explanation.summary: IAM users access the AWS Management Console using a username and password.
keyPoints: Credentials created during IAM user setup
explanation.additionalInfo: Console access for IAM users relies on username and password credentials. MFA is strongly recommended but not mandatory by default.

explanation.summary: Access keys are used for programmatic access, not console login.
explanation.why: Access keys authenticate API and CLI requests, not web console sessions.

questions.question: In your on-premises environment, you can create as many virtual servers as you need from a single template. What can you use to perform the same in AWS?

explanation.summary: IAM manages identities and permissions, not server templates.
explanation.why: IAM controls access to AWS resources but does not define or create compute templates.

explanation.summary: Internet gateways enable internet access, not instance replication.
explanation.why: They attach a VPC to the internet and do not create or manage compute instances.

explanation.summary: EBS snapshots back up volumes but do not define full server configurations.
explanation.why: Snapshots capture block storage data but do not include instance configuration, OS metadata, or launch settings.

explanation.summary: An AMI serves as a reusable template for launching EC2 instances.
keyPoints: Used to launch multiple identical instances
examples: Launching web servers from a golden image
Scaling EC2 fleets using Auto Scaling
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Machine Images are fundamental to EC2 operations. They allow consistent and repeatable server creation, similar to VM templates in on-premises environments.

questions.question: What are two advantages of using Cloud Computing over using traditional data centers? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Reserved capacity exists in both cloud and traditional environments.
explanation.why: Capacity reservation is not a unique advantage of cloud computing.

explanation.summary: Cloud architectures support built-in redundancy and fault tolerance.
explanation.additionalInfo: Cloud platforms enable elimination of SPOFs by design, without requiring physical infrastructure duplication by customers.

explanation.summary: Cloud computing provides globally distributed infrastructure.
examples: Serving global users from nearby regions
explanation.additionalInfo: Cloud providers operate globally distributed infrastructure, enabling designs that are impractical or cost-prohibitive in traditional data centers.

explanation.summary: Virtualization is not exclusive to cloud computing.
explanation.why: Traditional data centers can also use virtualization technologies.

explanation.summary: Dedicated hosting is not a core advantage of cloud computing.
explanation.why: Dedicated infrastructure exists in traditional environments as well.

questions.question: Which of the following aspects of security are managed by AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: EBS encryption configuration is customer-controlled.
explanation.why: AWS provides encryption capabilities, but customers choose whether and how to encrypt volumes.

explanation.summary: Customers configure VPC security controls.
explanation.why: Security groups and NACLs are managed by customers.

explanation.summary: IAM permissions are defined by customers.
explanation.why: AWS provides IAM, but customers manage policies and permissions.

explanation.summary: AWS manages patching of physical hardware.
keyPoints: Part of security of the cloud
explanation.additionalInfo: Customers never interact with physical hardware in AWS. Patching and maintenance are fully handled by AWS.

explanation.summary: AWS is solely responsible for securing its global infrastructure.
explanation.additionalInfo: Physical and environmental security are fully owned by AWS and are not exposed to customers.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the operational excellence pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.text: The ability of a system to recover gracefully from failure.

explanation.summary: This statement describes the Reliability pillar, not Operational Excellence.
explanation.why: Operational Excellence focuses on processes, monitoring, and continuous improvement. Recovery from failure is primarily addressed by the Reliability pillar.

options.text: The efficient use of computing resources to meet requirements.

explanation.summary: This statement aligns with the Performance Efficiency pillar.
explanation.why: Performance Efficiency focuses on selecting and using resources efficiently. Operational Excellence is about operations and improvement processes.

options.text: The ability to monitor systems and improve supporting processes and procedures.

explanation.summary: Operational Excellence emphasizes monitoring, automation, and continuous process improvement.
explanation.additionalInfo: The Operational Excellence pillar is about running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and continually improving processes and procedures. It encourages automation, small reversible changes, and learning from operational events.

options.text: The ability to manage datacenter operations more efficiently.

explanation.summary: AWS customers do not manage physical data centers.
explanation.why: Operational Excellence focuses on application and operational processes, not physical data center management.

questions.question: AWS has created a large number of Edge Locations as part of its Global Infrastructure. Which of the following is NOT a benefit of using Edge Locations?

options.text: Edge locations are used by CloudFront to cache the most recent responses.

explanation.summary: Caching content at edge locations is a core CloudFront benefit.
explanation.why: CloudFront caches content close to users to reduce latency and improve performance.

options.text: Edge locations are used by CloudFront to improve your end users' experience when uploading files.

explanation.summary: Edge locations can improve upload performance using services like S3 Transfer Acceleration.
explanation.why: Uploads can be accelerated by routing traffic through nearby edge locations.

options.text: Edge locations are used by CloudFront to distribute traffic across multiple instances to reduce latency.

explanation.summary: Traffic distribution across instances is handled by load balancers, not edge locations.
keyPoints: Edge locations cache and serve content
Do not balance traffic across EC2 instances
Load balancing is handled by ELB
Edge locations reduce latency through proximity
Different AWS services serve different roles
examples: Using ALB for instance traffic distribution
explanation.additionalInfo: Edge locations improve performance by serving cached content closer to users. They do not distribute traffic across backend compute resources, which is the responsibility of Elastic Load Balancing.

options.text: Edge locations are used by CloudFront to distribute content to global users with low latency.

explanation.summary: This is a primary benefit of edge locations.
explanation.why: CloudFront uses edge locations to deliver content with low latency worldwide.

questions.question: What are the change management tools that helps AWS customers audit and monitor all resource changes in their AWS environment? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS CloudTrail records API activity and account actions.
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudTrail is essential for governance and compliance. It provides visibility into account activity and is a core change auditing service in AWS.

explanation.summary: Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing service.
explanation.why: It analyzes text data and does not track or audit infrastructure changes.

explanation.summary: AWS Transit Gateway connects VPCs and networks.
explanation.why: It manages network connectivity, not configuration auditing.

explanation.summary: AWS X-Ray traces application requests.
explanation.why: X-Ray is used for application performance debugging, not infrastructure change management.

explanation.summary: AWS Config tracks resource configurations and changes over time.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Config complements CloudTrail by focusing on the state of resources rather than API calls, making both essential for full change visibility.

questions.question: Which of the following services allows you to run containerized applications on a cluster of EC2 instances?

explanation.summary: Amazon ECS is a managed container orchestration service for running containers on EC2 clusters.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon ECS simplifies container management by handling scheduling, placement, and lifecycle of containers on EC2. It removes the need to manage your own orchestration platform.

explanation.summary: AWS Data Pipeline is used for data workflow orchestration, not containers.
explanation.why: It schedules and moves data between AWS services but does not run containerized applications.

explanation.summary: AWS Cloud9 is a cloud-based IDE.
explanation.why: Cloud9 provides a development environment, not container execution or orchestration.

explanation.summary: AWS Personal Health Dashboard provides service health information.
explanation.why: It informs customers about AWS service events and does not run workloads.

questions.question: Which of the following services will help businesses ensure compliance in AWS?

explanation.summary: CloudFront is a content delivery network.
explanation.why: It improves content delivery performance but does not provide auditing or compliance tracking.

explanation.summary: CloudEndure Migration is used for workload migration.
explanation.why: It migrates servers to AWS but does not track or enforce compliance.

explanation.summary: CloudWatch provides monitoring and logging.
explanation.why: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs but does not provide audit trails for compliance.

explanation.summary: AWS CloudTrail records API activity for auditing and compliance.
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudTrail is a foundational compliance service that enables governance, risk, and audit capabilities across AWS accounts.

questions.question: Which of the following procedures will help reduce your Amazon S3 costs?

options.text: Use the Import/Export feature to move old files automatically to Amazon Glacier.

explanation.summary: AWS Import/Export is deprecated and not used for automated lifecycle transitions.
explanation.why: S3 Lifecycle policies are used to transition data between storage classes, not Import/Export.

options.text: Use the right combination of storage classes based on different use cases.

explanation.summary: Selecting appropriate S3 storage classes reduces costs.
keyPoints: Different storage classes for different access patterns
Lower cost for infrequently accessed data
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon S3 offers multiple storage classes optimized for cost and access frequency. Proper lifecycle management is a common exam topic and a real-world cost optimization strategy.

options.text: Pick the right Availability Zone for your S3 bucket.

explanation.summary: S3 is a regional service and does not require AZ selection.
explanation.why: Customers do not choose Availability Zones for S3 buckets.

options.text: Move all the data stored in S3 standard to EBS.

explanation.summary: EBS is more expensive and unsuitable for object storage.
explanation.why: EBS is block storage tied to EC2 and is not cost-effective for large object storage workloads.

questions.question: What are the AWS services/features that can help you maintain a highly available and fault-tolerant architecture in AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS Direct Connect provides private connectivity but does not directly improve availability.
explanation.why: Direct Connect improves network consistency, but high availability requires redundancy and scaling mechanisms.

explanation.summary: EC2 Auto Scaling maintains application availability by adjusting capacity automatically.
examples: Scaling web servers during traffic spikes
explanation.additionalInfo: Auto Scaling is a core service for building resilient architectures. It works closely with load balancers to ensure healthy capacity is always available.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic across healthy resources.
examples: Routing traffic to healthy EC2 instances
explanation.additionalInfo: Elastic Load Balancing is a fundamental component of fault-tolerant AWS architectures, often paired with Auto Scaling for resilience.

explanation.summary: CloudFormation automates infrastructure deployment but does not directly provide availability.
explanation.why: It helps define and deploy resources but availability depends on how those resources are architected.

explanation.summary: Network ACLs control traffic but do not improve fault tolerance.
explanation.why: They are security controls and do not provide redundancy or automatic recovery.

questions.question: Which of the following activities may help reduce your AWS monthly costs?

options.text: Enabling Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling for all of your workloads.

explanation.summary: Auto Scaling helps reduce costs by matching capacity to demand.
explanation.additionalInfo: Auto Scaling ensures that workloads only consume resources when needed, which directly impacts monthly AWS costs.

options.text: Using the AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) to load balance the incoming HTTP requests.

explanation.summary: NLB is not optimized for HTTP traffic.
explanation.why: Application Load Balancer is better suited for HTTP/HTTPS. NLB does not inherently reduce costs.

options.text: Removing all of your Cost Allocation Tags.

explanation.summary: Removing tags reduces visibility, not cost.
explanation.why: Cost allocation tags help track and optimize spending. Removing them does not reduce usage or cost.

options.text: Deploying your AWS resources across multiple Availability Zones.

explanation.summary: Multi-AZ improves availability, not cost reduction.
explanation.why: Deploying across AZs often increases cost due to additional resources.

questions.question: What is the AWS service/feature that takes advantage of Amazon CloudFront's globally distributed edge locations to transfer files to S3 with higher upload speeds?

explanation.summary: S3 Transfer Acceleration improves upload speeds using edge locations.
explanation.additionalInfo: S3 Transfer Acceleration leverages the AWS global network to speed up data transfers to S3 buckets, especially over long distances.

explanation.summary: AWS WAF protects applications but does not accelerate file transfers.
explanation.why: WAF filters web traffic and does not impact upload performance.

explanation.summary: AWS Snowmobile is used for massive offline data migration.
explanation.why: It physically transports data and is not used for accelerating online uploads.

explanation.summary: AWS Snowball is for offline data transfer.
explanation.why: Snowball devices move data physically and do not improve online upload speeds.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS security features is associated with an EC2 instance and functions to filter incoming traffic requests?

explanation.summary: AWS X-Ray is an application tracing service.
explanation.why: X-Ray analyzes request paths and latency but does not filter or block network traffic.

explanation.summary: Network ACLs operate at the subnet level, not the instance level.
explanation.why: NACLs are stateless and apply to subnets, whereas the question asks for an EC2 instance–associated feature.

explanation.summary: Security Groups act as virtual firewalls for EC2 instances.
keyPoints: Rules defined by protocol, port, and source
examples: Restricting SSH access by IP address
explanation.additionalInfo: Security Groups are one of the most tested AWS security concepts. They provide instance-level protection and automatically allow return traffic for allowed inbound requests.

explanation.summary: VPC Flow Logs capture network traffic metadata.
explanation.why: Flow Logs record traffic information but do not filter or block requests.

questions.question: Which AWS services can be used to improve the performance of a global application and reduce latency for its users? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS KMS manages encryption keys, not performance.
explanation.why: KMS provides key management and does not reduce application latency.

explanation.summary: AWS Global Accelerator improves global application performance.
explanation.additionalInfo: Global Accelerator directs user traffic to the nearest healthy endpoint using AWS edge locations, improving latency and availability for global applications.

explanation.summary: AWS Direct Connect improves private connectivity but not global user latency.
explanation.why: It benefits hybrid connectivity rather than internet-facing global users.

explanation.summary: AWS Glue is an ETL service.
explanation.why: Glue processes data but does not improve application latency.

explanation.summary: Amazon CloudFront reduces latency by caching content at edge locations.
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudFront is a core AWS service for global performance optimization and is frequently paired with S3, ALB, and API Gateway.

questions.question: Using Amazon RDS falls under the shared responsibility model. Which of the following are customer responsibilities? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Customers design and manage database schemas in Amazon RDS.
explanation.additionalInfo: While AWS manages the database infrastructure, customers retain full control and responsibility over database schemas and data models.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS performs automated backups.
explanation.why: RDS handles automated backups and snapshots when enabled.

explanation.summary: Customers manage database configuration settings in RDS.
explanation.additionalInfo: Customers control database parameters and configuration options, while AWS manages patching and infrastructure.

explanation.summary: Database engine patching is handled by AWS in RDS.
explanation.why: RDS automates patching of the database engine as part of the managed service.

explanation.summary: AWS installs and manages the database engine in RDS.
explanation.why: RDS abstracts database software installation as part of the service.

questions.question: A company has a large amount of structured data stored in their on-premises data center. They are planning to migrate all the data to AWS, what is the most appropriate AWS database option?

explanation.summary: Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database and not ideal for structured relational data.
explanation.why: DynamoDB is optimized for key-value and document data models and does not support complex relational queries.

explanation.summary: Amazon SNS is a messaging service.
explanation.why: SNS delivers notifications and does not store or query structured datasets.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS is designed for structured relational data.
keyPoints: Common choice for on-prem database migrations
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon RDS supports multiple relational engines and is the standard choice for migrating structured relational data from on-premises environments to AWS.

explanation.summary: Amazon ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, not a primary database.
explanation.why: ElastiCache is used for performance optimization and does not persist structured datasets long term.

questions.question: A company has created a solution that helps AWS customers improve their architectures on AWS. Which AWS program may support this company?

explanation.summary: APN Consulting Partners support customers with architecture and implementation services.
keyPoints: Helps customers design and optimize architectures
explanation.additionalInfo: APN Consulting Partners specialize in helping customers design, migrate, and optimize solutions on AWS, making this the most appropriate program.

explanation.summary: AWS TAM is a support role, not a partner program.
explanation.why: A Technical Account Manager supports customers directly but does not represent a company program.

explanation.summary: Technology Partners focus on building AWS-integrated products.
explanation.why: They create software products rather than providing architecture consulting services.

explanation.summary: AWS Professional Services is delivered directly by AWS.
explanation.why: It is not a partner program supporting third-party companies.

questions.question: What is the AWS serverless service that allows you to run your applications without any administrative burden?

explanation.summary: Amazon Lightsail provides simplified virtual servers.
explanation.why: Lightsail still requires server management and is not serverless.

explanation.summary: AWS Lambda runs code without provisioning or managing servers.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Lambda abstracts all infrastructure management, allowing developers to focus solely on application logic.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS manages databases, not application code execution.
explanation.why: RDS is not a compute service for running application logic.

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 requires server provisioning and management.
explanation.why: EC2 is not serverless and requires OS and infrastructure administration.

questions.question: Jessica is managing an e-commerce web application in AWS. The application is hosted on six EC2 instances. One day, three of the instances crashed; but none of her customers were affected. What has Jessica done correctly in this scenario?

options.text: She has properly built an elastic system.

explanation.summary: Elasticity focuses on scaling with demand, not absorbing failures.
explanation.why: The scenario describes continued availability despite failures, which is fault tolerance, not elasticity.

options.text: She has properly built a fault tolerant system.

explanation.summary: Fault tolerance allows systems to continue operating when components fail.
keyPoints: Failures do not impact end users
examples: Multiple EC2 instances behind a load balancer
Using Auto Scaling to replace failed instances
explanation.additionalInfo: Fault-tolerant architectures are designed so that component failures do not cause service disruption. This is a core AWS design principle and a frequent exam concept.

options.text: She has properly built an encrypted system.

explanation.summary: Encryption protects data, not availability.
explanation.why: Encryption has no impact on whether users experience downtime.

options.text: She has properly built a scalable system.

explanation.summary: Scalability handles growth, not failure recovery.
explanation.why: The scenario describes resilience to failures, not scaling capacity up or down.

questions.question: Where can you store files in AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Amazon EFS provides scalable file storage in AWS.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon EFS is designed for file-based workloads that require shared access across multiple instances.

explanation.summary: Amazon SNS is a messaging service.
explanation.why: SNS delivers notifications and does not store files.

explanation.summary: Amazon EBS provides persistent block storage for EC2.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon EBS volumes are commonly used for file storage within EC2 instances and support snapshots for backup and recovery.

explanation.summary: Amazon ECS is a container orchestration service.
explanation.why: ECS runs containers but does not store files itself.

explanation.summary: Amazon EMR is a big data processing service.
explanation.why: EMR processes data but relies on other services for storage.

questions.question: Which AWS service can be used to store and reliably deliver messages across distributed systems?

explanation.summary: Amazon SQS reliably stores and delivers messages between components.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon SQS is designed to ensure messages are not lost even if consumers fail, making it essential for resilient distributed architectures.

explanation.summary: AWS Storage Gateway integrates on-premises storage with AWS.
explanation.why: It provides hybrid storage, not messaging.

explanation.summary: Amazon SES is an email service.
explanation.why: SES sends emails and does not function as a message queue.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is an object storage service.
explanation.why: S3 stores files and objects but is not a messaging system.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the payment model that AWS makes available for customers that can commit to using Amazon EC2 over a one or 3-year term to reduce their total computing costs?

explanation.summary: This phrase refers to AWS economies of scale, not a pricing model.
explanation.why: AWS economies of scale describe long-term price reductions, not a customer commitment-based pricing option.

explanation.summary: Pay-as-you-go does not require long-term commitments.
explanation.why: This pricing model is flexible but does not provide the discounted rates associated with 1 or 3-year commitments.

explanation.summary: This describes volume-based pricing, not EC2 commitment discounts.
explanation.why: Using more resources does not guarantee EC2 commitment discounts without reservations or savings plans.

explanation.summary: Reserved pricing provides discounts for 1 or 3-year EC2 usage commitments.
examples: Reducing EC2 costs for stable applications
explanation.additionalInfo: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans offer significant cost savings compared to On-Demand pricing when workloads have predictable usage patterns.

questions.question: A company is migrating its on-premises database to Amazon RDS. What should the company do to ensure Amazon RDS costs are kept to a minimum?

explanation.summary: Right-sizing is important but not the correct answer for this specific question.
explanation.why: The question focuses on a specific architectural choice rather than a general optimization practice.

explanation.summary: An Active-Passive setup reduces cost by limiting active resources.
keyPoints: Only one region actively serves traffic
Secondary region used for disaster recovery
explanation.additionalInfo: Active-Passive architectures balance cost and availability by avoiding duplicated active workloads across regions, which significantly reduces database costs.

options.text: Combine On-demand Capacity Reservations with Saving Plans.

explanation.summary: This option applies to EC2, not Amazon RDS.
explanation.why: Capacity Reservations and Savings Plans do not directly apply to RDS pricing.

explanation.summary: Active-Active architectures increase cost.
explanation.why: Running multiple active databases across regions significantly increases operational expenses.

questions.question: What is the primary storage service used by Amazon RDS database instances?

explanation.summary: Amazon Glacier is designed for archival storage.
explanation.why: Glacier is not suitable for low-latency database workloads.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS uses Amazon EBS for database storage.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon RDS leverages Amazon EBS to provide reliable, high-performance storage while abstracting storage management from customers.

explanation.summary: Amazon EFS is a file storage service.
explanation.why: RDS does not use shared file storage for database engine data.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is object storage.
explanation.why: Databases require block storage rather than object storage.

questions.question: A company is developing a new application using a microservices framework. The new application is having performance and latency issues. Which AWS Service should be used to troubleshoot these issues?

explanation.summary: AWS CodePipeline is a CI/CD orchestration service.
explanation.why: CodePipeline manages software delivery workflows and does not analyze application performance or latency.

explanation.summary: AWS X-Ray helps analyze and troubleshoot performance and latency issues in distributed systems.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS X-Ray is purpose-built for monitoring and debugging distributed applications. It provides deep visibility into request paths, making it ideal for microservices architectures.

explanation.summary: Amazon Inspector performs security vulnerability assessments.
explanation.why: Inspector evaluates security posture and does not focus on performance or latency analysis.

explanation.summary: AWS CloudTrail records API activity for auditing.
explanation.why: CloudTrail tracks actions and changes, not application performance metrics.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services is designed with native Multi-AZ fault tolerance in mind? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Amazon Redshift does not provide native Multi-AZ fault tolerance by default.
explanation.why: Redshift primarily relies on cluster-based architecture and does not automatically replicate across AZs.

explanation.summary: AWS Snowball is a data transfer service.
explanation.why: It is used for offline data migration and does not provide fault-tolerant service availability.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is inherently multi-AZ and highly durable.
keyPoints: Designed for eleven nines of durability
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon S3 automatically replicates data across multiple Availability Zones within a region, making it one of the most resilient AWS services.

explanation.summary: Amazon EBS volumes are scoped to a single Availability Zone.
explanation.why: While durable, EBS volumes do not natively replicate across AZs.

explanation.summary: Amazon DynamoDB is designed for Multi-AZ high availability by default.
explanation.additionalInfo: DynamoDB replicates data synchronously across multiple AZs, ensuring high availability and durability without customer intervention.

questions.question: What are the Amazon RDS features that can be used to improve the availability of your database? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS Regions provide geographic separation, not an RDS availability feature.
explanation.why: Regions are part of global infrastructure but are not specific RDS features.

explanation.summary: Multi-AZ deployments provide automatic failover for RDS.
explanation.additionalInfo: Multi-AZ is the primary high-availability feature of Amazon RDS and is heavily tested in AWS certification exams.

explanation.summary: Automatic patching improves security and maintenance, not availability.
explanation.why: Patching reduces risk but does not directly provide high availability.

explanation.summary: Read Replicas improve availability and scalability for read-heavy workloads.
keyPoints: Can be promoted in some scenarios
explanation.additionalInfo: Read Replicas complement Multi-AZ deployments by improving read scalability and providing additional recovery options.

explanation.summary: Edge Locations are part of CloudFront, not RDS.
explanation.why: They are used for content delivery, not database availability.

questions.question: Sarah has deployed an application in the Northern California (us-west-1) region. After examining the application's traffic, she notices that about 30% of the traffic is coming from Asia. What can she do to reduce latency for the users in Asia?

options.text: Replicate the current resources across multiple Availability Zones within the same region.

explanation.summary: Using multiple Availability Zones improves availability, not global latency.
explanation.why: Availability Zones are within a single region. They do not reduce network distance for users in other continents.

options.text: Migrate the application to a hosting provider in Asia.

explanation.summary: Migrating away from AWS is unnecessary and not aligned with AWS best practices.
explanation.why: AWS provides global infrastructure and edge services that solve latency issues without changing providers.

explanation.summary: Recreating content does not address network latency.
explanation.why: Latency is caused by physical distance and network routing, not content structure.

options.text: Create a CDN using CloudFront, so that content is cached at Edge Locations close to and in Asia.

explanation.summary: Amazon CloudFront reduces latency by serving content from edge locations near users.
keyPoints: Caches content at global edge locations
examples: Serving static assets from Asian edge locations
Reducing page load time for global users
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudFront is the standard AWS solution for reducing global latency. It delivers content from the closest edge location, significantly improving user experience for geographically distributed audiences.

questions.question: An organization runs many systems and uses many AWS products. Which of the following services enables them to control how each developer interacts with these products?

explanation.summary: AWS IAM controls access and permissions for AWS resources.
examples: Restricting developer access to production resources
explanation.additionalInfo: IAM is the foundation of AWS security. It defines who can access which resources and what actions they can perform, making it essential for multi-user environments.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS is a managed database service.
explanation.why: RDS manages databases and does not control user access across AWS services.

explanation.summary: Network ACLs control network traffic, not user permissions.
explanation.why: NACLs filter traffic at the subnet level and do not manage developer access to AWS services.

explanation.summary: Amazon EMR is a big data processing service.
explanation.why: EMR processes data and does not provide identity or access management.

questions.question: Using Amazon EC2 falls under which of the following cloud computing models?

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 does not fall under SaaS.
explanation.why: EC2 provides infrastructure resources, not fully managed software applications.

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 is an Infrastructure as a Service offering.
explanation.additionalInfo: EC2 is the canonical example of IaaS in AWS, offering maximum control over compute resources short of physical hardware.

explanation.summary: SaaS delivers fully managed applications.
explanation.why: EC2 does not deliver ready-to-use software applications.

explanation.summary: PaaS abstracts infrastructure management.
explanation.why: EC2 requires customers to manage servers and operating systems, which is not PaaS.

questions.question: Which of the below is a best-practice when building applications on AWS?

options.text: Strengthen physical security by applying the principle of least privilege.

explanation.summary: Least privilege applies to access control, not physical security.
explanation.why: Customers do not manage physical security in AWS; that is AWS responsibility under the shared responsibility model.

options.text: Ensure that the application runs on hardware from trusted vendors.

explanation.summary: Hardware selection is handled by AWS, not customers.
explanation.why: AWS manages and secures the underlying hardware infrastructure.

options.text: Use IAM policies to maintain performance.

explanation.summary: IAM policies control access, not application performance.
explanation.why: Performance is influenced by architecture and resource selection, not permission management.

options.text: Decouple the components of the application so that they run independently.

explanation.summary: Decoupling improves scalability, resilience, and maintainability.
explanation.additionalInfo: Decoupling is a fundamental AWS architectural best practice. It allows systems to evolve independently and handle failures gracefully.

questions.question: Your company is designing a new application that will store and retrieve photos and videos. Which of the following services should you recommend as the underlying storage mechanism?

explanation.summary: Amazon EBS is block storage tied to EC2 instances.
explanation.why: EBS is not ideal for large-scale object storage like photos and videos.

explanation.summary: Amazon SQS is a messaging service.
explanation.why: SQS stores messages, not binary media objects.

explanation.summary: Instance store provides temporary storage.
explanation.why: Instance store data is lost when instances stop or terminate.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is designed for durable, scalable object storage.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon S3 is the standard AWS service for storing unstructured data such as photos and videos with high durability and scalability.

questions.question: Amazon Glacier is an Amazon S3 storage class that is suitable for storing [...] & [...]. (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Amazon Glacier is designed for archival data with infrequent access.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Glacier is optimized for data that is accessed rarely but must be retained for long periods at the lowest cost.

explanation.summary: Dynamic website assets require frequent and low-latency access.
explanation.why: Glacier retrieval times are too slow for dynamic content delivery.

explanation.summary: Long-term analytics data is well suited for archival storage.
explanation.additionalInfo: Glacier is commonly used for analytics data that must be retained but is rarely queried.

explanation.summary: Active databases require low-latency storage.
explanation.why: Glacier is not designed for active database workloads.

explanation.summary: Cached data requires fast access.
explanation.why: Glacier retrieval latency makes it unsuitable for caching.

questions.question: What does Amazon Elastic Beanstalk provide?

options.text: A PaaS solution to automate application deployment.

explanation.summary: Amazon Elastic Beanstalk is a Platform as a Service offering for deploying applications.
explanation.additionalInfo: Elastic Beanstalk allows developers to focus on writing code while AWS manages capacity provisioning, load balancing, and health monitoring.

options.text: A compute engine for Amazon ECS.

explanation.summary: Elastic Beanstalk does not act as a compute engine for ECS.
explanation.why: ECS uses EC2 or Fargate for compute, not Elastic Beanstalk.

options.text: A scalable file storage solution for use with AWS and on-premises servers.

explanation.summary: This describes Amazon EFS or Storage Gateway.
explanation.why: Elastic Beanstalk does not provide file storage services.

explanation.summary: Elastic Beanstalk is not a database service.
explanation.why: NoSQL databases are provided by services like DynamoDB.

questions.question: What is the AWS service that performs automated network assessments of Amazon EC2 instances to check for vulnerabilities?

explanation.summary: Amazon Kinesis is a data streaming service.
explanation.why: It processes streaming data and does not perform security assessments.

explanation.summary: Security groups control network access.
explanation.why: They filter traffic but do not assess vulnerabilities.

explanation.summary: Amazon Inspector automatically assesses EC2 instances for vulnerabilities.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Inspector helps improve security by automatically analyzing applications and EC2 instances for potential vulnerabilities.

explanation.summary: Network ACLs filter network traffic.
explanation.why: They do not perform vulnerability assessments.

questions.question: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following controls do customers fully inherit from AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Patch management responsibilities vary by service.
explanation.why: Customers still manage patching for applications and operating systems in many cases.

explanation.summary: Database controls are often shared or customer-managed.
explanation.why: Customers manage database configuration and access.

explanation.summary: Awareness and training are customer responsibilities.
explanation.why: Organizations must train their own staff.

explanation.summary: AWS fully manages environmental controls for its data centers.
explanation.additionalInfo: Environmental controls are fully inherited controls under the shared responsibility model and require no customer action.

explanation.summary: AWS is solely responsible for physical security controls.
explanation.additionalInfo: Physical security is fully managed by AWS and is a core inherited control for all customers.

questions.question: A company needs to host a database in Amazon RDS for at least three years. Which of the following options would be the most cost-effective solution?

explanation.summary: No Upfront Reserved Instances provide savings but not the maximum discount.
explanation.why: For long-term predictable usage, Partial Upfront typically offers better overall cost savings.

explanation.summary: Partial Upfront Reserved Instances provide the lowest effective cost for long-term RDS usage.
keyPoints: Best balance of upfront and ongoing cost
explanation.additionalInfo: For databases with predictable, long-term usage, Partial Upfront Reserved Instances usually deliver the maximum savings compared to No Upfront or On-Demand pricing.

explanation.summary: On-Demand pricing is the most flexible but also the most expensive long-term option.
explanation.why: On-Demand does not provide commitment-based discounts needed for multi-year workloads.

explanation.summary: Spot Instances are not supported for Amazon RDS.
explanation.why: RDS does not run on Spot capacity and requires stable, predictable compute resources.

questions.question: Your application has recently experienced significant global growth, and international users are complaining of high latency. What is the AWS characteristic that can help improve your international users' experience?

explanation.summary: Elasticity focuses on scaling resources based on demand.
explanation.why: Elasticity does not directly reduce network latency for global users.

explanation.summary: AWS global reach allows services to be delivered close to users worldwide.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS global infrastructure enables applications to be deployed closer to end users, which directly improves latency and performance for international audiences.

explanation.summary: Durability refers to data protection against loss.
explanation.why: Durability does not affect response times or latency.

explanation.summary: High availability ensures uptime.
explanation.why: Availability does not necessarily reduce latency for geographically distant users.

questions.question: Savings Plans are available for which of the following AWS compute services? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS Batch uses underlying compute services.
explanation.why: Savings Plans apply to the compute services themselves, not Batch directly.

explanation.summary: AWS Outposts pricing is separate from Savings Plans.
explanation.why: Outposts has its own pricing model and does not use standard Savings Plans.

explanation.summary: Lightsail uses simplified bundled pricing.
explanation.why: Savings Plans do not apply to Lightsail pricing.

explanation.summary: Savings Plans apply directly to Amazon EC2 usage.
explanation.additionalInfo: Compute Savings Plans provide significant discounts for EC2 usage in exchange for a consistent amount of compute usage over time.

explanation.summary: Savings Plans also apply to AWS Lambda compute usage.
explanation.additionalInfo: Compute Savings Plans cover both EC2 and Lambda, making them suitable for mixed compute architectures.
